security_spec.violation_condition: Kernel code computes a capability's top bound as saturating_add(GCBASE(cap), GCLEN(cap)) for access-control or bounds-enforcement decisions instead of using the GCTOP instruction, and the hardware's actual decoded top diverges from that software computation due to representable-format edge cases, saturation semantics mismatch, or future capability encoding changes.
security_spec.summary: Kernel that computes capability top as base+len (instead of using GCTOP) may enforce incorrect bounds if the hardware's decoded top diverges from the software computation, allowing userspace to bypass CHERI capability bounds checks.

findings.finding: This kernel tree (Linux 7.0-rc5) contains zero CHERI capability code. Searched for: GCBASE, GCLEN, GCTOP, CGetBase, CGetLen, CGetTop, YBASER, YLENER, YTOPER, YTOPR, saturating_add in arch/riscv — all returned no matches. The vulnerability pattern (software-computed top = saturating_add(base, len) instead of GCTOP instruction) cannot manifest because no capability bounds-checking code exists. The 'GCTOP' grep hits (tda18271, drxk_hard, etc.) are unrelated DVB tuner gain-control topology references. The 'capability' hits are Linux POSIX credentials (include/linux/capability.h), not CHERI hardware capabilities. Similarly, 'representable' hits are numerical overflow checks (include/linux/overflow.h), not CHERI representability checks.
findings.snippet: No relevant code found — CHERI capability support is absent from this kernel tree.
